Point and Speak engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume camera-point read-aloud capability covers storefront language. Xcode, camera APIs, and Connect actually separate Detection Mode behavior in the app from product-page copy:

  • Camera-point text recognition — on-device OCR, text detection in the camera viewfinder, and bounding boxes around physical text on signs or labels. Engineering inside the binary — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Point and Speak read-aloud playback — converting detected physical text to spoken audio when the user points the camera at a sign, menu, or label. Controls voice quality and speaking rate — does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Magnifier Detection Mode UI — Detection Mode toggle, Point and Speak control, and camera-point targeting reticle in Magnifier-style interfaces. Listing copy should match what screenshots actually show.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Point and Speak features in the app.

Working Point and Speak flows in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe Point and Speak, Detection Mode, and camera-point text reading on the product page in zh-Hans, not how you implement OCR or speech synthesis.

Point and Speak-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Point and Speak marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe camera-point text reading — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Point and Speak vs Magnifier zoom

US pages use "Point and Speak", "Detection Mode", or "Point at text and hear it read." China storefront copy often uses 指着说, 指向朗读, or 指读文字 — depending on whether you mean Apple's Magnifier Detection Mode Point and Speak or a third-party sign-reading app. Magnifier zoom copy uses 放大镜 or 阅读放大 — a different buyer story. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual feature scope.

Detection Mode vs generic camera apps

Screenshot galleries may label Magnifier Detection Mode: "Detection Mode", "Point at signs", or camera reticle demos over restaurant menus. zh-Hans overlay lines may use 检测模式, 指着说, or 指向朗读 — matching what your English gallery actually shows, not generic "best camera app" vocabulary.

Physical text vs on-screen read-aloud

Point and Speak reads text on physical objects the camera sees — signs, menus, product labels. Speak Screen and Speak Selection read text already on the device screen. Listing copy must not conflate 指着说 (point at physical text) with 朗读屏幕 (read on-screen content) unless your app genuinely ships both and your English listing already claims both accurately.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Point and Speak–relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 指着说, 指向朗读, and 指读文字 each signal different intent from magnifier zoom or screen-reader keywords.

Why English-only Point and Speak copy hurts China storefront conversion

Low-vision and senior purchasers browsing the China App Store evaluate camera-point reading claims in the first scroll. Common failure modes when only en-US is filled:

  • Trust gap — Chinese word-of-mouth recommends a "sign reader app"; buyer taps through and sees English "Point and Speak" with no zh-Hans context
  • Localized listing, English badges — description promises Chinese camera-point reading; screenshot overlays still "Detection Mode" at the worst moment
  • Search intent miss — buyers search 指着说 or 指向朗读; English-only keywords miss intent even when Point and Speak works in the app
  • Competitor contrast — rivals with native zh-Hans Point and Speak copy look more serious about China buyers who need physical-text reading help
  • Conflation with Magnifier zoom — machine-translated 放大镜 copy on a Point and Speak gallery frame misleads buyers expecting zoom, not spoken text detection

Clearer zh-Hans Point and Speak marketing reduces confusion on the product page. It does not replace OCR code, camera APIs, or in-app Detection Mode settings.
